final_mapped_build_native_offline.scope: Same compiled final policy including fixed user-message classification; native public certificate/cache-path and forced safe-unavailable HTTPS/HTTP/WSS checks only. The previous live network matrix was not repeated.

interpretation.application_additive_checks: Actual production key policy parsed/rejected all16 public certs/8SPKIs under JDK and Android. Synthetic verified-path providers returned a compromised intermediate absent from the peer list; wrapper rejection was verified through real Android X509TrustManagerExtensions. That provider is a test seam, not a replacement for real network trust.
interpretation.normal_endpoints: Airtap update metadata and example.com both returned HTTP200 with application policy; wrong hostname, expired chain and untrusted self-signed certificate remained rejected.
interpretation.reason: System public-key blocklist rejection, not a network timeout. This emulator already had the system mitigation; the added app policy must not receive credit for that default-platform rejection.
interpretation.unavailable_verifier: Empty connection specs and a pre-network denying interceptor allowed client construction while HTTP/HTTPS/WSS to a reserved .invalid hostname all failed with fixed policy error, before DNS.

limits: Native device scope is the isolated Android16/API36 emulator only; no physical phone, older Android trust store or personal-AI runtime validation.
Eight keys are blocked bySPKI across16 certificate representations. Live endpoints cover sixTLS intermediates and twoNoCT variants, not a live TLS endpoint for two code-signing-only intermediates.

System socket/engine verification runs first with its handshake context. A second host-aware verified-chain check may additionally reject future CT-enforcing configurations that only supply SCTs via TLS/OCSP; it does not weaken CT or use hidden APIs.
The live probe APK precedes only the final fixed user-facing security-error mapping; that mapping has type-classification host tests and compile/lint validation.
No active interception or compromised Airtap service was established.
